_comment: Favicon provenance. The CDN .ico is both the canonical artwork and the declared icon; the same-origin copy is the fallback.

cdn_hotlink_block.was: 403 Cloudflare error 1011 for any cross-site Referer, so the URL could not render as a page icon. Path-independent: it applied to every raster extension Hotlink Protection covers (gif/ico/jpg/jpeg/png/bmp) and not to svg or webp — which is the only reason the .svg nav logo ever worked.
cdn_hotlink_block.fix: A Cloudflare Configuration Rule sets hotlink_protection=off for /pacs008/*.
cdn_hotlink_block.side_effect: Hotlink Protection is now off for that whole prefix for any referrer, so those assets can be hotlinked by third parties. Narrowing it to this origin would need a WAF rule on http.referer instead.

fallback.why: Browsers request /favicon.ico at the site root regardless of declarations. Keeping it means that if the CDN blocks again the icon degrades to the identical image instead of disappearing — which is what happened the first time and took three attempts to diagnose.

apple_touch_icon.why: Not available on the CDN, and Safari does not accept SVG for apple-touch-icon — this is what was missing on iOS. Derived from frame [3] (256x256) of the canonical .ico, resized to 180x180 with alpha removed, because iOS composites it onto the home screen and ignores transparency.

replaced_stale_icon: The favicon.ico previously committed was a different, older logo — a teal sunburst rather than the current waves-and-sun mark — so the live root favicon was stale artwork as well as the declarations being broken.
note: The nav logo also loads from the CDN, deliberately. That was never the defect.
